chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Yunus, from Mu'awiyah, who said:
I asked about the salat of the two 'Eids, so he said: They are two rak'ahs; there is nothing before them nor after them, and there is no adhan in them nor iqamah.
He says twelve takbirs in them. He begins, says takbir, and opens the salat, then recites Fatihat al-Kitab.
Then he recites: “By the sun and its brightness.”
Then he says five takbirs, then says takbir and bows, so he has bowed with the seventh. He performs two sajdahs, then stands and recites Fatihat al-Kitab.
And: “Has there come to you the حديث of al-Ghashiyah?”
Then he says four takbirs, performs two sajdahs, recites the tashahhud, and gives salam.
He said: And thus did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم do.

key_terms.أَذَانٌ: the call to prayer, which is absent for this salat
key_terms.إِقَامَةٌ: the commencement call for congregational salat, also absent here
key_terms.الْغَاشِيَةِ: the surah recited in the second rak'ah after al-Fatihah
key_terms.تَكْبِيرَةً: a declaration of Allah's greatness; here referring to the additional takbirs in the prayer
key_terms.رَكْعَتَانِ: two rak'ahs; the required unit-count of this prayer
key_terms.صَلَاةِ الْعِيدَيْنِ: the salat of the two 'Eids, meaning the ritual prayer of 'Eid al-Fitr and 'Eid al-Adha
key_terms.فَاتِحَةَ الْكِتَابِ: Surat al-Fatihah, recited in each rak'ah
key_terms.وَالشَّمْسِ وَضُحَاهَا: the surah recited in the first rak'ah after al-Fatihah

ai.seo_question: How is the salat of the two 'Eids performed according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the manner of performing the salat of the two 'Eids, including the number of rak'ahs, the extra takbirs, and the recitations. It also states that there is no adhan or iqamah for it and attributes this practice to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, making it an important source for the jurisprudence of 'Eid prayer.
